<result>I have everything needed. Here is the complete analysis of all three taps.

---

## tap-bamboohr

**1. Base URL** — Constructed from config `subdomain`:
`https://api.bamboohr.com/api/gateway.php/{subdomain}/v1`
(One stream, `CustomReport`, uses a different host: `https://{subdomain}.bamboohr.com/api/v1/custom-reports/{report_id}`.)

**2. Auth** — HTTP **Basic auth**, confirmed. `BasicAuthenticator(username=config["auth_token"], password="foobar")` — the API key/token goes in as the username, password is any throwaway string. (BambooHR ignores the password.) Applied as the standard `Authorization: Basic base64(auth_token:foobar)` header. Headers also set `Content-Type`/`Accept: application/json`. There's a side helper (`utils.get_employee_fields_from_config`) that hits `/meta/fields` with the same Basic header to fetch field metadata at schema-build time.

**3. Pagination** — Mostly **single-page / none**. Most streams return the whole payload in one response. Two exceptions:
- `CustomReport` (the active custom-report stream) uses `CustomReportPaginator(BasePageNumberPaginator)` starting at page 1; `has_more` = `response.json()["pagination"]["next_page"] is not None`; the next page is sent as `?page=<n>`. Pages are 500 rows.
- Legacy POST streams (`CustomReportOld`, `PhotosUsers`) use `SinglePagePaginator`.

**4. Per-stream endpoints** (path appended to url_base, method, params, records JSONPath):

| Stream (name) | Path | Method | Params | Record extraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employment` (EmploymentHistoryStatus) | `/employees/changed/tables/employmentStatus` | GET | `since=2012-01-01T00:00:00Z` | **custom**: iterate `response.json()["employees"]` dict `{empId: {lastChanged, rows:[...]}}`, emit each row |
| `payroll` (CompensationHistory) | `/employees/changed/tables/compensation` | GET | `since=2012-01-01T00:00:00Z` | same custom employees-dict walk |
| `work` (JobInfo) | `/employees/changed/tables/jobInfo` | GET | `since=2012-01-01T00:00:00Z` | same custom employees-dict walk |
| `employee` (Employees) | `/employees/{_employee_id}` | GET | `fields=<comma list>&onlyCurrent=false` | default (single object) + heavy field-id→name remapping |
| `<custom>` (CustomReport) | `/custom-reports/{report_id}` (on `{subdomain}.bamboohr.com` host — but SDK request uses `url_base` path) | GET | `page=<n>` | `$.data[*]` |
| `whos_out` | `/time_off/whos_out` | GET | `start=1900-01-01&end=2100-12-12` | default |
| `time_off_requests` | `/time_off/requests` | GET | `start=1900-01-01&end=2100-12-12` | default, then flattens dict ignoring `dates` |
| `employee_assets` | `/employees/all/tables/employeeAssets` | GET | — | default |
| `locations_detail` | `/applicant_tracking/locations` | GET | — | `$[*]` |
| `photos_users` | `/reports/custom` | **POST** | `format=JSON`, body `{"name":"photos_users","fields":["id","isPhotoUploaded"]}` | `$.employees[*]` |
| `photos` | `/employees/{_sdc_id}/photo/{photo_size}` | GET | — | base64-encodes raw image bytes |
| list streams (`job_titles`,`locations`,`divisions`,`departments`,`employment_statuses`) | `/meta/lists` | GET | — | `$[?(@.alias=='<X>')].options[*]` (JSONPath filter expressions) |

**5. Incremental/replication key** — **None.** Every stream sets `replication_key = None`. "Incremental-style" tables use a hardcoded `since=2012-01-01` full pull, not state-driven. Full-refresh throughout.

**6. Non-trivial mechanics a generic HTTP+JSONPath+cursor source could NOT reproduce:**
- **`custom_reports` config** (`"31:employee_report,42:foo"`): parsed at discovery into dynamically-created `CustomReport` streams, one per `id:name`. Each **fetches one sample record at discovery time to infer its schema** (all fields typed `["null","string"]`) — dynamic per-report schema inference via a live API call.
- **`additional_streams` config**: comma-list that toggles optional streams on via a name→class `STREAM_MAPPING`.
- **Parent-child dependency**: `employee` stream is a **child of `employment`** — it iterates employee IDs discovered from the employmentStatus table and does **one GET per employee** (`/employees/{id}`), deduped via `_seen_employee_ids`. N+1 per-record child API calls.
- **`photos`/`photos_users`**: child stream doing per-employee photo GETs, returning **binary image data base64-encoded**, with 404-skip logic (`NoPhotoFound`).
- **Custom employees-dict response shape** (`{employeeId: {lastChanged, rows:[]}}`) — not a flat array; requires custom parsing per stream.
- **`/meta/fields` metadata call + field aliasing**: the `employee` stream dynamically extends its schema and query `fields` param from BambooHR field metadata, honoring `include_fields`/`exclude_fields` config with `id:alias` remapping, then remaps numeric field-ids in responses back to names, snake_cases, and sanitizes to BigQuery-legal column names (`%`→`percent`, etc.).
- **POST search endpoints** (`/reports/custom` with a JSON body of field lists).
- Data standardization: camelCase→snake_case key rewriting, nullifying `"0000-00-00"`/`""` temporal values, and `"true"`/`"false"` string→bool coercion.

---

## tap-rippling

**1. Base URL** — Literal constant: `https://api.rippling.com/platform/api`. (Token endpoint is on a different host — see below.)

**2. Auth** — **OAuth2 refresh_token grant** (`RipplingOAuthAuthenticator`):
- Token endpoint: **`https://api.rippling.com/api/o/token/`** (POST).
- Client credentials go in an `Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)` header (via `meltano_utils.auth.build_basic_auth_header`), `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
- Body: `grant_type=refresh_token`, `refresh_token=<config.refresh_token>`.
- The returned `access_token` is applied as the bearer on API calls; `expires_in` drives refresh timing.
- **Refresh-token rotation**: Rippling rotates the refresh_token on *every* refresh, so `update_access_token` writes the new `refresh_token` to `/tmp/refresh_token.txt` (`REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE`) for the next ECS run to pick up. Config keys: `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token`.

**3. Pagination** — **Offset/limit**, opt-in and conditional (only one stream). In `Employees.get_next_page_token`: if `page_size <= 0` (the default `0`) → single unpaginated request (returns `None`). If `page_size > 0`: params get `limit=page_size` and `offset=next_page_token`; the next token = `previous + page_size`, and it stops when a returned page has `< page_size` records (or isn't a list). No cursor field — pure offset arithmetic.

**4. Per-stream endpoints** — **Only one stream**, `employee`:
- Path: `/employees/include_terminated` (→ `https://api.rippling.com/platform/api/employees/include_terminated`), GET.
- Params: always `send_all_roles=true`; plus `limit`/`offset` when paginating.
- Records JSONPath: **`$.[*]`** (top-level array). (Base class default is `$.results[*]`, but Employees overrides to a bare array.)

**5. Incremental/replication key** — **None.** `primary_keys=["id"]`, no replication key. Full refresh.

**6. Non-trivial mechanics:**
- **Refresh-token rotation persisted to a file** across runs — a generic OAuth2-refresh source that doesn't write the rotated token back would break on the second run (Rippling invalidates the old refresh_token).
- Response standardization: recursive **camelCase→snake_case** key rename, dict flattening (with `ignore_keys=["work_schedule"]` preserved as nested), and timestamp cleanup (`fix_timestamp_keys` strips the `+00:00` offset by splitting on `+` for `created_at`/`updated_at`).
- **Not** catalog/discover-driven — despite being a Singer tap, streams are a static list of exactly one (`Employees`); no dynamic endpoint discovery. `page_size` is a workaround for Rippling's ~60s gateway timeout on large unpaginated pulls.

---

## tap-rillet

**1. Base URL** — Literal: `https://api.rillet.com`. Paths append directly (e.g. `/accounts`, `/reports/balance-sheet`).

**2. Auth** — **Static bearer token** (`BearerTokenAuthenticator(token=config["auth_token"])`) → `Authorization: Bearer <auth_token>`. No token exchange. Report streams also send header **`X-Rillet-API-Version: 3`** (required or dimension fields come back null). The on-the-fly partition-discovery helpers build the same `Authorization: Bearer` header manually with `requests`.

**3. Pagination** — **Cursor**. `next_page_token_jsonpath = "$.pagination.next_cursor"`; params `limit=100&cursor=<next_cursor>`; stops when `pagination.next_cursor` is absent. **Report streams disable pagination** (`next_page_token_jsonpath = None`) — they're point-in-time/period single responses, partitioned by date instead.
Rate limiting: 60 req/rolling-minute, 429 with **no** Retry-After header → custom `backoff.constant(interval=65s)`, max 8 tries (both on SDK streams and in the raw-`requests` helper `_get_with_rate_limit_retry`).

**4. Per-stream endpoints** (collection streams — GET, cursor-paginated):

| name | path | records JSONPath | notes |
|---|---|---|---|

# tap-hubspot (DrivetrainAi/tap-hubspot, `main`)

Custom Meltano SDK tap (`RESTStream` subclasses) but with almost every I/O method overridden — it bypasses the SDK request flow and calls its own `get_request`/`post_request` (in `utils/req.py`, `requests` + `backoff`). Config is OAuth (`client_id`/`client_secret`/`refresh_token`), `start_date`, and crucially `streams_to_discover` (comma-separated) plus BigQuery config (`bigquery_project/dataset/credentials_path/location`) — the tap talks to BigQuery directly (see §6).

**1. Base URL** — varies by stream (note two hosts, `api.hubspot.com` vs `api.hubapi.com`):
- Object streams: `https://api.hubspot.com/crm/v3/objects/{object_type}/search` (`streams/object.py` `url_base`).
- Property discovery: `https://api.hubspot.com/crm/v3/properties/{object_type}`.
- Associations: `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v4/associations/{from}/{to}/batch/read`; association types: `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/associations/{from}/{to}/types`.
- Property history: `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/{object_type}/batch/read`.
- List membership: `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/lists/{id}/memberships` (and `/crm/v3/lists/{id}` to resolve object type).

**2. Auth** — OAuth2 **refresh-token grant**. Token endpoint `POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v1/token`, form-encoded body `grant_type=refresh_token`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token`, `redirect_uri=https://api.hubspot.com/` (`auth.py`). Response `access_token`/`expires_in`; token cached, refreshed 600 s before expiry. Applied as header `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

**3. Pagination** — cursor via `paging.next.after`. Paginator (`TapHubspotPaginator`): `get_next` = `response.json()["paging"]["next"]["after"]`; `has_more` true while that is non-null. For object search, `after` is injected into the POST body (`payload["after"] = next_page_token`), not a query param. Archived listing paginates the same field via query param. **Non-trivial 10k cap workaround:** HubSpot search caps at ~10k results per filter; when `total_records_processed >= 9800` the stream adds a secondary `hs_object_id GT <last_id>` filter and resets the cursor to keep walking (see `prepare_request_payload`).

**4. ## Tap 1 — `tap-dynamics-business-central` (MS Dynamics 365 Business Central)

Two modes. **Default = "standard API" multi-company** (`standard_api.py`); legacy OData-v4 mode is opt-in via `use_legacy_odata_v4: true` (`client.py` + `streams.py`).

**1. Base URL construction**
- **Standard mode** (`_url_base_for` / `_company_url`, standard_api.py:131, 183): literal template
  `https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/v2.0/{tenant}/{environment}/{namespace}/companies({company_id})/{entity}`
  where `namespace` = `api/v2.0` (core) or `api/microsoft/reportsFinance/beta` (opt-in budgets). `{environment}` may be a comma-separated list (`Production,Sandbox`) — it fans out. `{company_id}` is a GUID enumerated at runtime from `GET .../api/v2.0/companies` (`_fetch_companies`, :676).
- **Legacy mode** (`url_base`, client.py:24): `override_base_url` wins if set; else
  `https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/v2.0/{tenant}/{environment}/ODataV4`, with an optional `/Company('{company}')` suffix (single-quotes doubled for OData escaping).

**2. Auth flow** — Azure AD OAuth2 **client-credentials (v2.0)**.
- Token endpoint (auth.py:41, and duplicated in `_get_token` standard_api.py:471): `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token`
- Body: `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, **`scope=https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/.default`** (v2.0 `.default` scope — not a `resource` param).
- Bearer applied as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Token cached on the tap (`_cached_bc_token`); metadata fetches build the header manually because the SDK auth lifecycle isn't invoked during schema discovery (client.py:176).

**3. Pagination** — body `@odata.nextLink` (`get_next_page_token`, client.py:62 / standard_api.py:835). The nextLink is a full URL used **verbatim** (`prepare_request` bypasses url_base rebuild, :850). Page size is controlled by the **`Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=N`** request header (`http_headers`, :820), default `page_size=100`, overridable per-stream (GL entries pinned to `BC_MAX_PAGE_SIZE=20000`). No `$skip`/`$top`.

**4. Per-entity requests**
- Records JSONPath: **`$.value[*]`**.
- Entity catalog is hardcoded (`TOP_LEVEL_ENTITIES`, standard_api.py:346): tuples `(bc_entity_name, pk_field, expand_lines, namespace)`. Path = `/companies({company_id})/{bc_entity_name}`.
- **`$expand`** is heavily used: header/line entities (salesInvoices→`salesInvoiceLines`, journals→`journalLines`, GL→`dimensionSetLines`, etc.) pull nested lines inline via `?$expand=<lines>`; expands are trimmed to `$select=id` where metadata confirms the field, else untrimmed (`_expand_clause`, :153).
- `$orderby` used in legacy mode (replication_key asc + PKs). Each record annotated with `company_id`/`company_name`/`environment`; keys camelCase→snake_case.
- In standard mode `entities_to_sync` filters the fixed catalog by **snake_case** names; in legacy mode it selects raw OData EntitySet names.

**5. Incremental key** — only `generalLedgerEntries` is incremental (`STREAM_REPLICATION_KEYS = {"generalLedgerEntries": "lastModifiedDateTime"}`, :293). Filter built in `get_url_params` (:967): `{field} ge {YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ}` from state bookmark/`start_date`, but only if start > the `DEFAULT_START_DATE = 2010-01-01` floor. Legacy mode (client.py:126) uses `{replication_key} gt {start}` where replication_key is auto-detected (`lastModifiedDateTime`/`systemModifiedAt`). Plus optional **inclusive range filters** for GL: `accountNumber ge/le '...'` (quoted) and `postingDate ge/le ...` (bare Edm.Date), ANDed together (`_filter_clauses`, :947).

**6. Not reproducible by a generic REST source**
- **Runtime company enumeration + fan-out**: one `GET /companies` then every stream is partitioned across every (environment, company); `company` config is a case-insensitive filter over name/displayName/GUID that hard-fails on no match.
- **EDMX `$metadata` schema discovery** at `/{namespace}/$metadata` (XML→schema), unioned across environments; opt-in beta namespace tolerated-absent.
- **Per-(company,entity) fault tolerance**: 403/404 and specific BC 400 envelopes (`Application_DialogException`, `Internal_DataNotFoundFilter`, etc.) downgraded to empty result so one company can't fail the run.
- **Parent-child enumeration for `journal_lines`**: BC refuses top-level journalLines, so it paginates `/journals` per company first, then requests `/journals({jid})/journalLines` per journal.
- **Composite PK injection** `(entity_pk, company_id[, environment])`, `dimensionSetLines` stringified to JSON, 429 Retry-After handling, memory reclaim of ~23MB pages. A plain authenticated-GET + `$.value[*]` + nextLink source handles a *single* company/entity but none of the multi-company orchestration, metadata discovery, or selective fault tolerance.

---

## Tap 2 — `tap-dynamics-finance` (MS Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations)

**1. Base URL construction** (`url_base`, client.py:107): `base_url` wins → `{base_url}/data`; else `subdomain` → `https://{subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com/data`; else raises. All entities live under the single `/data` OData root.

**2. Auth flow** — Azure AD OAuth2, but **v1 endpoint + `resource` param** (older ADAL-style), *not* v2.0 `.default`.
- Token endpoint (auth.py:72): `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/token` (or `.../common/oauth2/token` if no tenant). **Note: v1 `/oauth2/token`, not `/oauth2/v2.0/token`.**
- Body (auth.py:29): `client_credentials` grant with **`resource=https://{subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com`** (subdomain derived from config or stripped from `base_url`). Alternatively supports a **`refresh_token` grant** (client_id/secret/redirect_uri/refresh_token) if `refresh_token` is configured.
- Bearer via the SDK `OAuthAuthenticator`; `SingletonMeta` shares one authenticator per run, guarded by a `threading.Lock` (`authenticate_request`, :24) because of concurrent partitioned fetching.

**3. Pagination** — server-driven body `@odata.nextLink` via a proper SDK `BaseHATEOASPaginator` (`ODataNextLinkPaginator`, client.py:54). The nextLink is **offset-based `$skip`/`$top` under the hood** but server-generated and preserves the original `$filter`; on each page the tap replays the nextLink's own query string (`get_url_params` → `parse_qsl(next_page_token.query)`, :168). Page size via **`Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=10000`** header (:135). Explicitly warns *not* to use `$top` for page size (it caps the total set and would truncate).

**4. Per-entity requests**
- Records JSONPath **`$.value[*]`**; `$format=json` always appended; **`cross-company=true`** always set (queries across all legal entities/`dataAreaId`).
- `entities_to_sync` is a comma-separated list, each item optionally `EntitySet:stream_name` (colon override; tap.py:105). Path = `/{object_name}`.
- Optional company scoping: if `company` set and `dataAreaId` is a PK → `$filter=dataAreaId eq '{company}'`.
- **`$count`** is used for reconciliation (`get_source_count`: adds `$count=true&$top=0`, reads `@odata.count`, :278). `$select`/`$orderby`/`$top=1` used in key-bound discovery for partitioning.

**5. Incremental key** — auto-detected `SysModifiedDateTime` (client.py:880). Filter (`get_url_params`, :185): lower bound `SysModifiedDateTime gt {start}` (from bookmark/`start_date`) **AND** an upper bound `SysModifiedDateTime lt {fetch_start_time}` — `_fetch_start_time` is captured at sync start (:288) so the window is closed and stable, preventing rows written mid-run from moving the bookmark past unread data. Timestamps rendered `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`.

**6. Not reproducible by a generic REST source** — this tap is the most complex:
- **Source `$count` reconciliation**: after each stream it fetches OData `$count` over the exact sync filter and compares against distinct-PK count extracted; a shortfall beyond tolerance (`source_count_recon_tolerance_pct`, floored at 100 rows) raises `SilentTruncationError` and fails the tap (recon.py) — guards against offset-paging silently truncating a full-table overwrite. Configurable enforce/exclude/tolerance knobs.
- **Concurrent partitioned key-range extraction** (`partitioned_streams`): for FULL_TABLE single-integer-PK streams, discovers `(min,max)` PK via `$orderby+$top=1`, asserts no rows fall outside the window, tiles `[low,high)` into N half-open ranges, fetches them across a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (per-thread `requests.Session`) with a bounded queue for backpressure, and reconciles each key-window against `$count`. Emission stays serial; any range that fails/never-reports aborts so a partial snapshot can't overwrite a good table.
- **EDMX `$metadata` discovery** at `/data/$metadata` with a dedicated 429/Retry-After retry budget (honours HTTP-date or delay-seconds).
- **Closed upper-bound incremental window**, v1 `resource`-based OAuth, `cross-company` semantics, thread-safe singleton auth. faucet's oauth2 provider would need the **v1 `resource` grant shape**, and none of the recon/partitioning/count-window logic exists in a generic source.

---

## Tap 3 — `tap-sap` (SAP Business One Service Layer)

Simplest of the three (`streams.py` + `tap.py` only; no separate auth/client module).

**1. Base URL construction** (`url_base`, streams.py:90): `https://{host}:{port}/b1s/v1` — built from `host` + `port` config (e.g. `https://sl-eqnx.datacore.com.br:50000/b1s/v1`). Entity path = `{url_base}/{object_name}`.

**2. Auth flow** — **Service Layer `/Login` session-cookie**, not a bearer token (`SapB1Authenticator(AuthBase)`, :25).
- Login: `POST https://{host}:{port}/b1s/v1/Login` with JSON body `{"CompanyDB": company_db, "UserName": username, "Password": password}` (`_login`, :40).
- Response JSON carries `SessionId` (and `SessionTimeout`). The session id is cached at **module level** in `_SESSION_CACHE`, keyed by `(host, port, company_db, username)`, so all streams share one login.
- Every request carries the cookie header (`__call__`, :64): **`Cookie: B1SESSION={session_id}; CompanyDB={company_db}`**. (`verify_ssl` toggles TLS verification for self-signed certs.)
- **Session expiry / re-login**: minimal — `__call__` only logs in when the cache key is absent; there is **no 401/session-timeout detection or automatic re-login** once a session is cached. (SAP B1 sessions expire ~30 min idle; a long sync relies on the session staying alive.) `$metadata` fetch has its own `_get_session_cookie` that logs in the same way.

**3. Pagination** — body `@odata.nextLink` (`get_next_page_token`, :108), checking **both `odata.nextLink` and `@odata.nextLink`** keys (SAP B1 emits the un-prefixed form in some versions), and resolving relative links against `url_base` via `urljoin`. Page size via **`Prefer: odata.maxpagesize={page_size}`** header, default 500 (:98). SAP B1 Service Layer uses server-driven paging (`$skip`-based nextLink) — the tap follows the link verbatim and does **not** compute `$skip`/`$top` itself. (Note: SAP B1 also supports a `B1S-PageSize` header / `$skip` paging; this tap relies purely on the returned nextLink.)

**4. Per-entity requests**
- Records JSONPath **`$.value[*]`**.
- `entities_to_sync` comma-separated EntitySet names, optional `EntitySet:stream_name` colon override (tap.py:78). Path = `/{object_name}`.
- Optional **`$select`** only (`get_url_params`, :123) — from a class-level `select_columns` list (not exposed in config by default, so normally no params). **No `$filter`, no `$count`, no `$orderby`.**
- Records are flattened (`flatten_dict`) and keys snake_cased (`convert_keys_to_snake_case`) — nested ComplexType objects flattened with `_` join; arrays kept as arrays.

**5. Incremental key** — **none.** `replication_key = None` always (streams.py:503). Every stream is FULL_TABLE; no date filter is built. (SAP B1 objects do carry `UpdateDate`/`UpdateTime` but this tap does not use them.)

**6. Not reproducible by a generic REST source**
- **The `/Login` session-cookie handshake itself**: a POST-with-credentials that returns `SessionId`, then a `Cookie: B1SESSION=...; CompanyDB=...` on every subsequent GET. This is the biggest gap — faucet's static-bearer / oauth2 / token-endpoint providers all model `Authorization` headers from a token grant; none does a **JSON login → Set-Cookie/JSON-session-id → cookie header** flow, nor carries the paired `CompanyDB` cookie. A faucet `token_endpoint` provider could POST the login, but it would need to (a) read `SessionId` from the JSON body and (b) inject it as a **`Cookie` header** (two cookies), not `Authorization`.
- **Dual nextLink key handling** (`odata.nextLink` *and* `@odata.nextLink`) + relative-URL resolution.
- **Self-signed TLS opt-out** (`verify_ssl=false`) applied to every request incl. pagination and metadata.
- **EDMX `$metadata` discovery** with ComplexType/Collection expansion and schema flattening to match the flattened record shape.
- Session **expiry is unhandled**, so any faucet reimplementation should add re-login on 401 (an improvement over the tap).

---

### Cross-tap summary for faucet-stream gaps
- **BC & F&O** are Azure-AD OAuth2 client-credentials — faucet's `oauth2` provider covers **BC** directly (v2.0 `/oauth2/v2.0/token` + `scope=.../.default`). **F&O needs the v1 `/oauth2/token` + `resource=` grant shape** — verify faucet's oauth2 provider can emit a `resource` param (v1/ADAL style), otherwise that's a provider gap.
- **All three** use `$.value[*]` extraction + `@odata.nextLink` body pagination + `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` — faucet's REST source `NextLinkInBody` pagination + a `Prefer` header covers the happy path.
- **SAP B1** is the real outlier: **session-cookie `/Login` auth** (JSON login → `B1SESSION`+`CompanyDB` cookies) — no faucet auth provider models this; it's the primary replication blocker.
- **Genuinely non-REST-reproducible logic** (would be lost in a naive port): BC's runtime multi-company fan-out + `$metadata` schema discovery + per-partition 4xx tolerance + parent/child journal enumeration + `$expand` line inlining; F&O's `$count` completeness reconciliation, closed-window incremental filter, and concurrent PK-range partitioning. These are stateful/orchestration features beyond "authenticated GET + extract + paginate."</result>

LIMIT n`, but with real engineering around Redshift's lack of indexes/cursors: **keyset pagination** on a unique key when one exists, else **LIMIT/OFFSET** ordered by all columns, plus an optional **CTAS staging table** with a `ROW_NUMBER()` window (`_dt_rn`) for stable paging, and page-level reconnect/retry. This is pagination/reliability plumbing, not exotic protocol — semantically it's `SELECT ... FROM table` with a replication key.

**Verdict:** faucet `source-redshift` reproduces this cleanly — it is standard SQL-over-Postgres-wire with table selection and incremental replication keys. The only thing not 1:1 is the tap's bespoke ROW_NUMBER/CTAS-staging keyset pagination strategy, but that is an internal performance detail, not a capability a source connector needs to expose.

---

## tap-sharepointsites (onedrive mode)

**Token refresh — exactly as described.** In `client.py`'s `authenticator`, the `mode == "onedrive"` branch does an OAuth2 **refresh_token** grant against the common Azure AD endpoint:
```python
elif mode == "onedrive":
    refresh_token = self.config.get("refresh_token")
    client_id = self.config.get("client_id")
    client_secret = self.config.get("client_secret")
    ...
    token_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token"
    response = requests.post(token_url, data={
        "client_id": client_id,
        "client_secret": client_secret,
        "refresh_token": refresh_token,
        "grant_type": "refresh_token",
        "scope": "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default offline_access",
    })
    ...
    access_token = token_data["access_token"]
    # Microsoft rotates the refresh token on each use (logs redact the new value)
return BearerTokenAuthenticator.create_for_stream(self, token=access_token)
```
(The `sharepoint` mode instead uses `azure.identity.ClientSecretCredential`.) Note Microsoft **rotates the refresh token on every use** — the tap logs that a new one was issued but relies on the caller to persist it.

**File reads via Microsoft Graph, then blob parsing.** `file_stream.py` uses Graph base `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` and resolves items via `/me/drive/items/{file_id}` (personal OneDrive: hostnames `onedrive.live.com` / `-my.sharepoint.com`) or `/drives/{drive_id}/items/{file_id}` (SharePoint), with a name-search fallback (`/me/drive/root/search(q=...)`). Content is downloaded from `/me/drive/items/{id}/content` (or the SharePoint `@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl`), streamed with `Range`/prefix support for big files. The downloaded **blob** is then parsed by a format handler:
- `CSVHandler` → `csv.DictReader` over the text content.
- `ExcelHandler` → `openpyxl.load_workbook` over the bytes (with header detection, timeseries unpivot, date coercion).

So it is unambiguously a **file-download-and-parse** tap (CSV/Excel blobs), not a JSON record API.

**Verdict:** faucet `source-rest` + `faucet-auth` `oauth2_refresh` can reproduce the Azure AD refresh_token grant (including refresh-token rotation) and the Graph metadata calls, **but CANNOT reproduce the file-blob download + CSV/Excel parsing** (`csv.DictReader` / `openpyxl` workbook parsing, header/timeseries handling). That belongs to faucet's file/format sources (e.g. `source-csv`/`source-parquet` family), not `source-rest`; there is no Graph-driven "download an .xlsx from OneDrive and unpivot it" path in the REST/auth stack.</result>

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* — most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token — a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

This is a technical capability-audit report for the team — utilitarian, information-dense, scannable. I'll design it accordingly: a considered slate/teal palette with semantic status colors, monospace for configs, clear hierarchy, both themes token-driven. Let me write it.

faucet-stream · capability audit

Replicating 13 Meltano taps — the faithful build and the real gaps

Every tap in DrivetrainAi/meltano_taps ships the same two sinks — a JSONL debug loader and the z3z1ma BigQuery loader. This audit reproduces each tap's exact underlying mechanism in faucet-stream, marks precisely where faucet can't match it 1:1, and notes where faucet can do it better.

13 taps read to source 6 faithful / partial (REST + SQL) 4 hard blockers sink parity via write_mode: overwrite (#492, shipped)

Verdict at a glance

Which taps replicate, and what stops the rest

“Faithful” means the tap's real transport, auth, pagination and record shape reproduce exactly in a faucet config. “Partial” means the bulk/collection streams replicate but specific streams need a transform or hit a gap. “Blocked” means a core mechanism has no faucet equivalent today.

Faithful — direct replica Partial — core replicates, edges gapped Blocked — a core mechanism has no equivalent
TapSource systemTransportAuthfaucet sourceVerdictHeadline gap
redshiftAmazon RedshiftSQL (PG wire)DB user/passredshiftFaithful—
deelDeelREST/JSONStatic bearerrestPartialgross-to-net unpivot; 2-level child chain
rilletRilletREST/JSONStatic bearerrestPartialreport streams: computed month×dimension matrix
personioPersonioREST/JSONLogin → bearerrest + token_endpointPartialreport pivot; {value} unwrap; schema discovery
bamboohrBambooHRREST/JSONBasic (key as user)restPartialemployees-dict walk; N+1 child; custom reports
ripplingRipplingREST/JSONOAuth2 refreshrest + oauth2_refreshPartialrefresh-token rotation must persist across runs
hubspotHubSpot CRMREST/JSON (POST search)OAuth2 refreshrest + oauth2_refreshPartialPOST-body cursor+filter; property discovery; in-tap BQ delete
ms365bcDynamics 365 BCOData v2Azure AD v2 (.default)rest + oauth2Partialmulti-company fan-out; $metadata; $expand lines
ms365fnoDynamics 365 F&OODataAzure AD v1 (resource=)rest + ⚠authPartialv1 resource grant; $count recon; PK-range partitioning
sapSAP Business OneOData (Service Layer)Session cookierest + ✗authBlocked/Login → B1SESSION+CompanyDB cookie flow
onedriveOneDrive (MS Graph)File downloadOAuth2 refresh✗ noneBlockeddownload + parse CSV/Excel blobs (not a JSON API)
adpADP Workforce NowREST/JSONOAuth2 + mTLSrest + ✗mTLSBlockedmutual-TLS client certificate on every request
netsuiteNetSuite (SuiteQL)REST (SuiteQL POST)OAuth1 TBA (HMAC)rest + ✗authBlockedOAuth1 request signing; in-tap BigQuery deletes

The shape of every replica is identical: a source (rest, redshift) → two sinks in a topology — jsonl (the debug loader) and bigquery with write_mode: overwrite (matching the loaders' overwrite: true) or upsert (matching dedupe_before_upsert). The BigQuery overwrite is now bucket-free (#492). Per-entity streams become matrix rows; parent→child streams become parent: fan-out. Shared tokens live in the auth: catalog.

The reusable shape

One template pattern, four auth flavors

Nine of the thirteen fit a single faucet template shape. Here is the canonical REST→dual-sink replica; each tap below is a delta on this.

archetype — REST (bearer/oauth2) → JSONL + BigQuery(overwrite)

version: 1
name: deel_to_bq
params:
  auth_token: { type: string, required: true, secret: true }
  project_id: { type: string, required: true }
  dataset_id: { type: string, required: true }
# parent/child + per-entity streams fan out as matrix rows
matrix:
  - id: people
    source: { config: { path: "/people", records_path: "$.data[*]" } }
  - id: legal_entities
    source: { config: { path: "/legal-entities",
        pagination: { type: NextLinkInBody, next_link_path: "$.page.cursor" } } }
pipeline:
  source:
    type: rest
    config:
      base_url: "https://api.letsdeel.com/rest/v2"
      auth: { type: bearer, config: { token: "${param.auth_token}" } }
      records_path: "$.data[*]"
  nodes:            # topology = one source, two sinks (the tap's two loaders)
    jsonl:   { type: sink, kind: jsonl,
              config: { path: "./out/${row}.jsonl" } }
    bigquery: { type: sink, kind: bigquery,
              config: { project_id: "${param.project_id}", dataset_id: "${param.dataset_id}",
                       table_id: "${row}", batch_size: 5000,
                       write_mode: overwrite } }   # = loader overwrite: true, bucket-free

Auth flavors, all covered by the  auth: catalog

  • Static bearer — deel, rillet → type: bearer
  • Basic (key-as-user) — bamboohr → type: basic, username: ${key}
  • OAuth2 client-credentials — ms365bc, adp → oauth2 (.default scope)
  • OAuth2 refresh — hubspot, rippling, onedrive → oauth2_refresh
  • Custom login→token — personio → token_endpoint (token_path: $.data.token)

Auth flavors with no equivalent

  • OAuth1 HMAC signing — netsuite (TBA). No OAuth1 provider.
  • Session cookie — sap (B1SESSION+CompanyDB). Providers emit Authorization, not a dynamic Cookie.
  • Azure AD v1 resource= — ms365fno. oauth2 sends scope not resource; token_endpoint posts JSON not form.
  • mutual TLS — adp. The rest source's HTTP client takes no client cert/key.

Tap by tap

Exact mechanism, faithful replica, and the gaps

redshift

Amazon Redshift · SQLFaithful
Transport
Postgres wire (psycopg2); Redshift speaks PG.
Auth
host / port / db / user / password.
Streams
tables = list of schema.table; columns via SELECT … LIMIT 0.
Replication
FULL_TABLE or INCREMENTAL on a replication key (keyset paging).

  • Nothing structural. The bespoke ROW_NUMBER/CTAS keyset pagination is an internal perf detail, not a capability the source must expose.

faucet does it better

  • BigQuery write_mode: overwrite is atomic + bucket-free; no in-tap staging.

https://api.letsdeel.com/rest/v2
Auth
static bearer auth_token.
Pagination
per-stream: cursor $.page.cursor, offset, or single-page.
Records
$.data[*]. No incremental (full refresh).

Can't replicate 1:1

  • gross-to-net unpivot: response is a map of dynamic column keys → cell objects; the tap pivots to a tall row per (report, row, column) — needs a sql/wasm transform, not JSONPath.
  • Two-level child chain legal_entities → reports → gross_to_net: faucet parent: fan-out chains the requests, but only one level of ${parent.path} is idiomatic — 2 levels needs nested matrix rows.

faucet does it better

  • Collection streams (people, legal_entities) are a clean faithful replica.
  • The unpivot is reusable as a shared sql transform across Deel/Personio/HubSpot.

rillet

Rillet · REST (accounting)Partial

https://api.rillet.com

static bearer + header X-Rillet-API-Version: 3.

cursor $.pagination.next_cursor; reports disable paging.
Rate limit
60/min, 429 w/o Retry-After → constant 65s backoff.

Can't replicate 1:1

  • Report streams = a computed request matrix. Month-end / month-range windows from start_date, cross-producted with subsidiary & custom-field dimensions whose id lists are fetched at plan time from other endpoints. This is discovery-driven fan-out, not static matrix or pagination.
  • Deep report-tree flattening (sections→groups→accounts→balances) with rolled-up-leaf reconciliation — a bespoke walk.

faucet does it better

  • ~14 collection streams replicate faithfully (cursor + custom header).
  • The month-window part maps to ${now.*} + a backfill window; only the discovered-dimension cross-product is the true gap.

personio

Personio · REST (HR)Partial
Base URL
https://api.personio.de (v1 + v2 paths)
Auth
POST /v1/auth {client_id,client_secret} → {success,data.token} → bearer.
Pagination
v2 cursor (_meta.links.next), v1 offset.

Can't replicate 1:1

  • Report pivot (v1 custom reports): groups history cells by date and pivots one column per attribute_id — envelope transformation.
  • {value: X} unwrapping + dynamic_*→customfield_<label> rename via a second /custom-attributes call; dynamic schema from a sample.

faucet does it better

  • Auth replicates exactly via token_endpoint (body: {client_id,client_secret}, token_path: $.data.token).
  • The {value} unwrap is a 3-line sql transform.

bamboohr

BambooHR · REST (HR)Partial
Base URL
…/api/gateway.php/{subdomain}/v1
Auth
HTTP Basic — auth_token as username, throwaway password.
Pagination
mostly single-page; custom reports page-number.
Records
varies ($.data[*], $[*], JSONPath filters). No incremental.

Can't replicate 1:1

  • employees-dict shape ({empId:{rows:[…]}}) needs a custom walk, not an array JSONPath.
  • N+1 child calls: one GET /employees/{id} per id; photo streams return base64 image bytes.
  • Dynamic custom-reports + /meta/fields schema remapping + POST report endpoints.

faucet does it better

  • Basic auth + simple streams (whos_out, time_off, list metadata) replicate directly.
  • List streams' JSONPath-filter extraction ($[?(@.alias=='X')]…) is native to the rest source.

rippling

Rippling · REST (HR)Partial
Base URL
https://api.rippling.com/platform/api
Auth
OAuth2 refresh at /api/o/token/; Basic client header.
Pagination
offset/limit (opt-in via page_size); one stream (employees).
Records
$[*]. No incremental.

Can't replicate 1:1

  • Refresh-token rotation persistence. Rippling rotates the refresh_token on every refresh; the tap writes the new one to disk for the next run. faucet's oauth2_refresh rotates in-memory but doesn't persist across separate runs → the 2nd scheduled run would 401.

faucet does it better

  • Single-run replica is exact; camelCase→snake_case is a keys_case transform.
  • Fixing rotation-persistence in oauth2_refresh (write rotated token to the state store) also fixes onedrive.

HubSpot CRM · RESTPartial
Base URL
api.hubspot.com/crm/v3 + api.hubapi.com/crm/v4

faucet does it better

  • Auth via oauth2_refresh; the property flatten is a sql transform.

Azure AD v1 /oauth2/token + resource=… (form-encoded).

@odata.nextLink (server $skip) + maxpagesize=10000.

closed window: SysModifiedDateTime gt start AND lt run-start.

Base URL
https://{host}:{port}/b1s/v1
Auth

Every request

  • Session-cookie handshake. Login returns a SessionId carried as two cookies — faucet's providers all emit an Authorization header from a token grant. No provider does JSON-login → dynamic Cookie header.

  • The OData read path is otherwise a clean replica; a new session-cookie auth provider unblocks it (and would add 401 re-login the tap lacks).

https://api.eu.adp.com

Can't replicate 1:1

  • Mutual-TLS client certificate. ADP requires a client cert + key attached to every request. The rest source's HTTP client exposes no client-cert / identity config — hard blocker.

Reads

csv.DictReader / openpyxl (Excel), header detection, timeseries unpivot.

  • It is a file source, not a record API. It downloads CSV/Excel blobs from Graph and parses them. The rest source reads JSON responses; it can't fetch a binary and run a CSV/Excel reader over it.

Which taps replicate, and what stops the rest

archetype — REST (bearer/oauth2) → JSONL + BigQuery(overwrite)

version: 1
name: deel_to_bq
params:
  auth_token: { type: string, required: true, secret: true }
  project_id: { type: string, required: true }
  dataset_id: { type: string, required: true }
# parent/child + per-entity streams fan out as matrix rows
matrix:
  - id: people
    source: { config: { path: "/people", records_path: "$.data[*]" } }
  - id: legal_entities
    source: { config: { path: "/legal-entities",
        pagination: { type: NextLinkInBody, next_link_path: "$.page.cursor" } } }
pipeline:
  source:
    type: rest
    config:
      base_url: "https://api.letsdeel.com/rest/v2"
      auth: { type: bearer, config: { token: "${param.auth_token}" } }
      records_path: "$.data[*]"
  nodes:            # topology = one source, two sinks (the tap's two loaders)
    jsonl:   { type: sink, kind: jsonl,
              config: { path: "./out/${row}.jsonl" } }
    bigquery: { type: sink, kind: bigquery,
              config: { project_id: "${param.project_id}", dataset_id: "${param.dataset_id}",
                       table_id: "${row}", batch_size: 5000,
                       write_mode: overwrite } }   # = loader overwrite: true, bucket-free

It reproduces each of the 13 taps' exact mechanism, marks where faucet can't match it 1:1, and where faucet does it better. Headlines:

content.text:
Both of your instincts are right, and the code backs them up — I was drawing the line too conservatively. Here's the corrected picture.

## 1. Transforms — yes, a large share of the "gaps" aren't gaps

Transforms run on records *after* fetch, and faucet has `flatten` / `keys_case` / `cast` / `explode` built-ins plus **`sql` (DuckDB)** and **`wasm`** for arbitrary reshaping. Every "gap" I flagged that is really just *response shape* collapses into a transform:

| Tap · stream | The "gap" | Actually |
|---|---|---|
| hubspot | `properties.*` → `property_*` flatten | `flatten` / `sql` |
| personio | `{value: X}` unwrap; report pivot | `sql` (UNPIVOT/PIVOT) or `wasm` |
| deel | gross-to-net tall-table unpivot | `sql` UNPIVOT |
| bamboohr | employees-dict `{id:{rows:[]}}` walk | `explode` + `sql`, or `wasm` |
| rillet | report-tree (sections→accounts) flatten | `sql` / `wasm` |
| rippling | camelCase→snake_case; timestamp cleanup | `keys_case` + `cast` |

So those taps aren't "partial because of response shape" — they're **faithful `rest` replicas + a transform**. That's a real reclassification: the transform layer already covers them.

## 2. SAP — you're exactly right, it's not a blocker

The `token_endpoint` auth provider **already** does what you describe: POST to an external endpoint, extract the token from the JSON response by `token_path`. For SAP that's literally `POST /Login {CompanyDB,UserName,Password}` → `token_path: $.SessionId`. That part works today.

The *only* missing piece is **where the token gets placed**. Right now `token_endpoint` hardcodes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, but SAP needs it as `Cookie: B1SESSION=<id>; CompanyDB=<db>`. And here's the thing — faucet's `Credential` enum **already has a `Header { name, value }` variant**, and the `rest` source **already applies it as an arbitrary header** (`Credential::Header → Auth::Custom{headers}`). The plumbing exists end-to-end; `token_endpoint` just always emits `Bearer` instead of letting you configure the output header.

So SAP moves from **Blocked → small, well-scoped enhancement**: add an optional output-header template to `token_endpoint`, e.g.

```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${param.pass}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as: { header: "Cookie", template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}" }  # NEW
```

That ~10-line change also unblocks **ms365fno** (same provider, just needs to POST form-encoded with `resource=` instead of JSON) — so my two "auth gap" verdicts both shrink to one small `token_endpoint` enhancement.

## What's left that transforms + token_endpoint genuinely *can't* fix

These are pre-fetch / transport concerns (transforms are post-fetch; token_endpoint is a token fetch, not per-request signing or a TLS layer):

- **adp — mutual-TLS client cert.** The HTTP client itself must present a cert on every request. Real connector work.
- **netsuite — OAuth1 per-request HMAC signing.** Not a token fetch — every request is signed. Needs an OAuth1 signer.
- **onedrive — download + parse CSV/Excel blobs.** Can't even fetch the record; it's a file, not JSON.
- **hubspot — cursor + filter inside the POST *body*.** A pagination-style gap (faucet puts the cursor in query/next-link).
- **rillet reports / bc companies — discovery-driven request fan-out** (dimensions fetched at plan time).
- **rippling/onedrive — rotated refresh-token persistence** (small: write the rotated token to state).

So the **real** blocker list drops from 4 to effectively **2 hard (mTLS, OAuth1) + 1 file-source**, with SAP/F&O and all the response-shape items reclassified as "already doable" or "tiny enhancement."

Want me to (a) **update the artifact** to reflect this sharper taxonomy (transform-solvable / small-auth-enhancement / genuine-connector-gap), and (b) file just the **genuinely-hard** set as issues — `token_endpoint` custom-header output, mTLS on rest, OAuth1 provider, HTTP/Graph file source, POST-body pagination, refresh-token persistence?

content.text:
Verified against the code — here's the honest, per-case answer. Built-in transforms confirmed: `flatten {separator}`, `rename_keys {pattern: <regex>, replacement}`, `keys_case`, `cast` (Integer/Float/Bool/String/Timestamp, with `on_error: null`), `explode {path}`, `select`/`drop`/`set`/`rename_field`, and `records_path` uses `jsonpath_rust` (so `$.*` object-value wildcards work). No wasm anywhere below.

## Solvable with **built-ins only** (no SQL)

**rippling** — camelCase→snake + timestamp cleanup
```yaml
transforms:
  - { type: keys_case, config: { mode: snake } }
  - { type: cast, config: { field: created_at, to: timestamp } }
```

**hubspot** — `properties.{name}` → `property_{name}` + type coercion
```yaml
transforms:
  - { type: flatten, config: { separator: "_" } }              # properties_{name}
  - { type: rename_keys, config: { pattern: "^properties_", replacement: "property_" } }
  - { type: cast, config: { field: property_hs_createdate, to: timestamp, on_error: null } }  # epoch→ISO; ""→null
```

**personio** — `{value: X}` unwrap (the whole point of `rename_keys` being regex)
```yaml
transforms:
  - { type: flatten, config: { separator: "__" } }             # {field}__value
  - { type: rename_keys, config: { pattern: "__value$", replacement: "" } }
```

**bamboohr employees-dict** `{empId: {rows:[…]}}` — extraction is built-in:
```yaml
source: { config: { records_path: "$.*" } }   # object-value wildcard → each {rows:[…]}
transforms:
  - { type: explode, config: { path: rows } }  # → one record per row
```
⚠️ **Honest caveat:** `$.*` drops the object *key* (the employee id). If a row doesn't already carry the id inside it, re-attaching the key is **not** built-in → SQL (or accept it's missing). Everything else here is built-in.

**Bounded nested lines** (BC `salesInvoice`→`invoiceLines`, and any fixed-depth tree) — chained `explode` keeps the header fields on each line. Built-in, as long as the depth is known.

**Generic** — `""→null`, `"true"/"false"→bool`, epoch→ISO, stringify scalars → all `cast` / `value_case`.

## Needs **SQL** — built-ins genuinely can't (not washing over it)

| Case | Why no built-in |
|---|---|
| **personio report pivot** (rows → one column per `attribute_id`) | Pivot = grouping + column generation. No built-in produces columns from row values. → DuckDB `PIVOT`. |
| **deel gross-to-net unpivot** (object of *dynamic keys* → one row per key) | `explode` only lengthens **arrays**; nothing turns arbitrary object **keys** into rows. → DuckDB `UNPIVOT` / `unnest`. |
| **bamboohr field-id → field-name** remap (via `/meta/fields`) | A data-driven **lookup/join** to a reference table. `rename_keys` is a static regex, not a value lookup. → SQL reference relation (or keep numeric ids). |
| **BC `dimensionSetLines` → JSON string** | `cast: string` stringifies scalars, not objects. → SQL `to_json` (minor). |

## The one I **won't** pretend either solves

**rillet report-tree flatten** — if the hierarchy is truly *arbitrary depth* (sections→groups→subgroups→…→accounts→balances with denormalized ancestor totals + rolled-up-leaf reconciliation), that's recursive. Built-ins can't; SQL only awkwardly (a recursive CTE per page, and the rolled-up-leaf logic is bespoke). If the depth is actually **fixed** (~4 levels, which it likely is), chained `explode` + `set` is built-in. So: **built-in if bounded, genuinely hard if not** — I'd confirm the real depth before promising either.

## The important boundary (so SQL doesn't get over-credited)

Transforms — built-in **or** SQL — only reshape records **after** they're fetched. They do **nothing** for the request/auth-side gaps:

- **rillet report fan-out** (discover subsidiaries/custom-fields from other endpoints, then cross-product month windows) — that's request generation, no transform touches it.
- **hubspot POST-body cursor**, **adp mTLS**, **netsuite OAuth1 signing**, **onedrive file-blob parsing**, **SAP/F&O auth placement** — all pre-fetch. SQL is irrelevant to these.

So: of the response-shape items, **rippling, hubspot, personio, and most of bamboohr are pure built-in transforms**; **personio-report-pivot, deel-unpivot, bamboohr-field-lookup need SQL**; **rillet-report-tree is the genuine edge**. Want me to fold this built-in / SQL / hard split into the artifact's per-tap cards so the report reflects it?

input.command:
cd /Users/c-sikawats/Documents/GitHub/Personal/faucet-stream
gh auth switch --user PawanSikawat >/dev/null 2>&1
R=faucet-hq/faucet-stream
: > /tmp/ovw_issue_urls.txt

U1=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label feature --label tier-2 \
 --title "source-rest: mutual-TLS client-certificate auth" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Let the `rest` (and `xml`/`graphql`) HTTP sources present a **client certificate + private key** (mutual TLS) on every request, including the auth token request. Configurable from inline PEM, a file path, or a `${secret:…}`/`${vault:…}` reference.

## Motivation
ADP Workforce Now (and other enterprise/gov APIs) require mTLS: the client must present a certificate the server validates. faucet's `reqwest`-based HTTP sources have no client-cert/identity config today, so ADP cannot be replicated at all — it is one of only three hard blockers in the tap-replication audit. Ties to the Primary Goal (be the fastest, most-capable way to move data between endpoints) and Third-Party Connector Friendliness.

## Proposed design
Add an optional `tls` block to the REST source config (and mirror on xml/graphql):
```yaml
source:
  type: rest
  config:
    base_url: "https://api.eu.adp.com"
    tls:
      client_cert: "${secret:adp_cert_pem}"      # PEM (cert chain), inline / file:/ secret
      client_key:  "${secret:adp_key_pem}"       # PEM private key
      # or: client_identity_pkcs12 + password
      min_version: "1.2"                          # optional
```
- Build a `reqwest::Identity` (from PEM pair or PKCS#12) once in `new()` and attach it to the shared `reqwest::Client` (`ClientBuilder::identity`). Requires the `reqwest` `native-tls`/`rustls-tls` identity feature — pick the one already enabled and gate behind a `mtls` crate feature if it pulls new deps.
- The identity must apply to **all** requests the source makes (data + any token-endpoint call). If the token is obtained via a shared `auth:` provider, the provider's HTTP client also needs the identity — decide whether mTLS lives on the source's client only (ADP applies the cert to both the token and data requests, so the provider path matters).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/config.rs` (+ `stream.rs` client build), `crates/source/xml`, `crates/source/graphql`; possibly `crates/auth` if the token request must also present the cert; `crates/core` re-exports if a shared TLS config type is introduced.

## Edge cases
Encrypted private keys (passphrase); PKCS#12 vs PEM; cert chain vs leaf; `verify_ssl:false` self-signed servers (see the separate flag); secret redaction of key material in logs/errors.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source configured with a client cert/key completes a request against an mTLS-requiring endpoint (integration test via a wiremock/rustls server requiring client auth).
- Key material is never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the config/build path.
- Docs + README updated.

## Out of scope
Server-cert pinning; per-request rotating certs.

## References
Meltano tap replication audit; tap-adp (`cert=(pub,priv)` on token + data requests). Blocks: **adp**. Related sink work: #492.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -vE '_encode|_decode' | tail -1); echo "1 $U1" | tee -a /tmp/ovw_issue_urls.txt

U2=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label feature --label tier-2 \
 --title "faucet-auth: OAuth1 (HMAC-SHA256) request-signing provider" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Add an OAuth1 (one-legged, HMAC-SHA256) auth provider to `faucet-auth`, signing **each request** with consumer key/secret + token key/secret + realm, generating a per-request nonce/timestamp and the OAuth1 `Authorization` header.

## Motivation
NetSuite Token-Based Auth (TBA) is OAuth1 with HMAC-SHA256 — every SuiteQL/REST request carries a signature over the request method+URL+params. faucet-auth today only issues OAuth2 bearer tokens (`static`/`oauth2`/`oauth2_refresh`/`token_endpoint`), which model a *token* applied as a header, not **per-request signing**. So NetSuite cannot be replicated — one of three hard blockers in the tap audit. This is distinct from the `token_endpoint` provider: there is no token to fetch; the credential is computed fresh per request from the URL+method.

## Proposed design
The current `AuthProvider` returns a `Credential` once per token lifetime — OAuth1 needs to sign per request, so this needs a request-signing hook, not just a credential fetch. Options:
1. A new `RequestSigner` capability the HTTP sources call with `(method, url, query)` to produce the `Authorization` header — added as a defaulted trait method / optional provider capability so existing providers are unaffected.
2. Provider config:
```yaml
auth:
  netsuite:
    type: oauth1
    config:
      signature_method: HMAC-SHA256
      consumer_key: "${secret:ns_consumer_key}"
      consumer_secret: "${secret:ns_consumer_secret}"
      token: "${secret:ns_token_key}"
      token_secret: "${secret:ns_token_secret}"
      realm: "${param.account_upper}"   # NetSuite account, uppercased, - -> _
```
Reuse a maintained crate for the signature base string + HMAC (e.g. `oauth1-request` / hand-rolled HMAC-SHA256 over the RFC 5849 base string). NetSuite specifics: HMAC-**SHA256** (not the SHA1 default), realm case-sensitivity, POST body params (SuiteQL) excluded from the signature base as NetSuite expects.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/` (new `oauth1.rs` + `build_provider` arm), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` / `traits.rs` (per-request signing hook, defaulted), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (invoke the signer per request), `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (register the type).

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source with an `oauth1` provider produces a valid RFC 5849 HMAC-SHA256 `Authorization` header verified by a test double; signature stable for fixed nonce/timestamp (unit-tested pure signer).
- Secrets never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the pure signing path.
- Docs + README.

## Out of scope
Three-legged OAuth1 (request/authorize/access token dance); RSA-SHA1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-netsuite uses `requests_oauthlib.OAuth1Session` + `SIGNATURE_HMAC_SHA256`. Blocks: **netsuite** (SuiteQL). NetSuite also self-loads to BigQuery — replaced by native `write_mode` (#492), tracked separately if needed.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -vE '_encode|_decode' | tail -1); echo "2 $U2" | tee -a /tmp/ovw_issue_urls.txt

U3=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label feature --label tier-2 \
 --title "File source: fetch + parse CSV/Excel from an authenticated HTTP/Graph URL" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
A way to **download a file (CSV/Excel) from an authenticated HTTP endpoint** (e.g. Microsoft Graph `/drive/items/{id}/content`) and parse it into records — either by extending `source-csv`/`source-parquet` to accept an authed remote URL, or a small dedicated Graph/HTTP file source.

## Motivation
OneDrive (and SharePoint "files mode") are **not** JSON record APIs — the tap authenticates to Microsoft Graph, downloads an .xlsx/.csv **blob**, and parses it (`openpyxl`/`csv.DictReader`) with header/timeseries handling. The `rest` source reads JSON responses; it cannot fetch a binary and run a CSV/Excel reader over it. So OneDrive is unreplicable — the third hard blocker in the tap audit. faucet already parses CSV/Parquet from local + S3/GCS; the missing piece is fetching the blob over an authed HTTP/Graph URL.

## Proposed design
Preferred: extend the existing file sources with a remote fetch:
```yaml
source:
  type: csv           # (or a new `http-file`)
  config:
    url: "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{id}/items/{item}/content"
    auth: { ref: graph_onedrive }     # reuse faucet-auth (oauth2_refresh)
    format: excel                     # csv | excel
    # sheet, header_row, delimiter, glob-over-a-listing-endpoint, etc.
```
- Reuse `oauth2_refresh` for the Graph token (with rotation persistence, tracked separately).
- Excel parsing needs a reader crate (`calamine` is the standard Rust .xlsx/.xls reader) behind a feature flag.
- Support a listing step (Graph folder search) → one record-stream per matched file, or pair with `matrix` for known file ids.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/csv/` (remote fetch + optional excel via `calamine`), or a new `crates/source/http-file/`; `faucet-auth` reuse; docs + capability matrix; CI `feature-check` matrix if a new feature/crate is added.

## Edge cases
Large files (stream/range download); header detection; Excel multi-sheet + type coercion; Graph download-URL redirects (`@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl`); refresh-token rotation (see linked issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fetch + parse a CSV and an XLSX from an authed URL (wiremock serving fixture bytes) into the expected records.
- ≥90% patch coverage on the pure parse path; docs + README.

## Out of scope
Arbitrary binary formats beyond CSV/Excel; write-back to the file store.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-sharepointsites onedrive mode (Graph `/content` + `openpyxl`/`csv`). Blocks: **onedrive** (+ SharePoint files). Depends on refresh-token rotation persistence.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -vE '_encode|_decode' | tail -1); echo "3 $U3" | tee -a /tmp/ovw_issue_urls.txt

U4=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label enhancement --label tier-2 \
 --title "faucet-auth token_endpoint: custom output header (cookie) + form-encoded body / resource param" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Extend the existing `token_endpoint` auth provider so the fetched token can be placed in **any header** (not only `Authorization: Bearer`) and so the token request can be **form-encoded** and carry extra params (e.g. `resource=`). The provider already POSTs to an arbitrary endpoint and extracts the token via `token_path`; this is the last mile.

## Motivation
Two taps need auth flows that are *almost* covered today:
- **SAP Business One** (`tap-sap`): `POST /b1s/v1/Login {CompanyDB,UserName,Password}` returns a `SessionId` that must be carried as **`Cookie: B1SESSION=<id>; CompanyDB=<db>`** on every request — not an `Authorization` header. `token_endpoint` already fetches the id (`token_path: $.SessionId`), and `faucet_core::auth::Credential::Header { name, value }` **already** exists and the REST source already applies it as an arbitrary header. The provider just hardcodes `Credential::Bearer`.
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): Azure AD **v1** `/oauth2/token` with a **form-encoded** body containing `resource=https://{host}`. `oauth2` sends `scope` not `resource`; `token_endpoint` currently posts **JSON** (`req.json(body)`), which the OAuth token endpoint rejects.

Both reduce to small, additive knobs on `token_endpoint`. This is what reclassified SAP from "blocked" to "small enhancement" in the tap-replication audit.

## Proposed design
Add optional config to `token_endpoint` (`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs`):
```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${param.pass}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as:                                    # NEW; default = Authorization: Bearer {token}
        header: "Cookie"
        template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}"
  fno:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/token"
      encoding: form                               # NEW; default = json
      body: { grant_type: client_credentials, client_id: "…", client_secret: "…", resource: "https://${param.subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com" }
      token_path: "$.access_token"
```
- `apply_as` → return `Credential::Header { name, value }` (already applied by `rest`) with `{token}` substituted; default keeps `Credential::Bearer`.
- `encoding: form|json` → `req.form(body)` vs `req.json(body)`.
- Optional: re-auth on a 401 (SAP sessions expire ~30 min; the tap has no re-login — faucet can be better here).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs` (config + apply + encoding), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` (already has `Credential::Header`), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (already maps `Credential::Header` → `Auth::Custom`; verify multi-header/cookie value passes through), docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `token_endpoint` provider can emit the token as a configurable `Cookie` header and post a form-encoded body with a `resource` param (unit tests around the pure request-build + credential-shape).
- Secrets redacted; ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope
Full session lifecycle management beyond re-auth-on-401.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-sap `/Login`, tap-dynamics-finance v1 `resource=`. Unblocks: **sap, ms365fno**. `Credential::Header` already exists in `crates/core/src/auth.rs`.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -vE '_encode|_decode' | tail -1); echo "4 $U4"

U5=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label enhancement --label tier-2 \
 --title "faucet-auth oauth2_refresh: persist the rotated refresh_token to the state store" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
When an OAuth2 provider (e.g. Microsoft, Rippling) **rotates the refresh_token** on each refresh, `oauth2_refresh` must persist the new refresh_token durably so the *next* run authenticates. Today rotation is handled in-memory only, so a second scheduled run 401s.

## Motivation
- **Rippling** (`tap-rippling`): rotates the refresh_token on every refresh; the tap writes the new one to `/tmp/refresh_token.txt` for the next ECS run. A faucet `oauth2_refresh` provider that rotates in-memory works for one run but the next run presents the now-invalidated original → 401.
- **OneDrive** (`tap-sharepointsites` onedrive mode): same — Microsoft rotates the refresh_token each use.

This is a reliability gap: single-run replicas pass, scheduled/repeated runs fail. Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability).

## Proposed design
- Give `oauth2_refresh` an optional durable store hook so it can write the rotated `refresh_token` (and expiry) back. Reuse the pipeline's `StateStore` (the same durable backend used for bookmarks) under a dedicated key, e.g. `auth:oauth2_refresh:<provider-name>`.
- On startup, read the stored refresh_token (if present) in preference to the config's seed value; on each rotation, atomically persist the new one.
- Must be safe across concurrent rows sharing one provider (single-flight already exists) and across process restarts.
- Config: opt-in `persist: true` (or automatic when a state store is configured), referencing the run's state backend.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/oauth2.rs` (`OAuth2RefreshProvider`), a bridge to `faucet_core::StateStore`, `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (wire the state backend into provider construction), docs.

## Edge cases
Provider shared by N matrix rows (persist once, single-flight); first run with only a seed token; store unavailable (fail closed vs warn); secret redaction of the persisted token.

## Acceptance criteria
- A simulated rotating token endpoint: run 1 rotates + persists; run 2 (fresh process/provider) reads the persisted token and authenticates (integration test with a wiremock rotating endpoint + a file/memory state store).
- Token never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the persistence path.

## Out of scope
Non-rotating providers (unaffected); OAuth1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rippling `REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE`, tap-sharepointsites onedrive rotation. Unblocks: **rippling, onedrive**.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -vE '_encode|_decode' | tail -1); echo "5 $U5"

U6=$(gh issue create --repo $R --label enhancement --label tier-2 \
 --title "source-rest: POST-search pagination (cursor + filter in the request body)" \
 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Add a REST pagination style for **POST search** endpoints where the next-page cursor (and the incremental filter) live **in the request JSON body**, not in a query param or a next-link. The paginator must inject the extracted cursor back into the body for the next request.

## Motivation
- **HubSpot CRM** (`tap-hubspot`): reads objects via `POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search` with a JSON body `{filterGroups, limit, sorts, properties, after}`; the next cursor is `$.paging.next.after` and is placed back into `payload.after`. The incremental filter (`hs_lastmodifieddate GTE …`) is also in the body. faucet's `rest` source supports POST + body, but its pagination styles (Cursor/PageNumber/Offset/LinkHeader/NextLinkInBody) all advance a **query param or next-link**, not a body field.
- **NetSuite SuiteQL** (`tap-netsuite`) posts `{"q":"SELECT …"}` with offset/limit — a related body-driven pattern (though offset there is a URL param).

Without this, HubSpot's core object streams can't paginate faithfully.

## Proposed design
A new `PaginationStyle::CursorInBody` (name TBD) on the REST source:
```yaml
pagination:
  type: CursorInBody
  next_token_path: "$.paging.next.after"     # where the next cursor is read from the response
  body_cursor_field: "after"                 # where to write it into the next request body
  # stops when next_token_path is null/absent; loop-guard on repeated token (as Cursor does)
```
- Reuse the existing cursor loop-detection + `max_pages` cap.
- The initial body comes from `source.config.body`; each subsequent request sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`.
- Consider a companion for HubSpot's 10k-result `hs_object_id GT <last>` re-filter (a secondary body mutation when a page count threshold is hit) — could be a follow-up.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/pagination/` (new module + `PaginationStyle` variant + `advance` handling that mutates the body), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (thread the body mutation into the next request), docs (pagination table in `.claude/rules/connectors.md` + the docs site).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock POST-search endpoint returning `paging.next.after` paginates to completion, injecting the cursor into the body each page; loop guard + `max_pages` honored. Unit + integration tests.
- ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope
GraphQL (has its own source); the HubSpot 10k re-filter (separate follow-up); dynamic property discovery (separate).

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-hubspot object search. Unblocks: **hubspot** (core objects); related: **netsuite** SuiteQL. Pagination styles: `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.
EOF
